common_name: Kathy Ann Azalea (White-Flowered Girard Evergreen Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Kathy Ann is a compact Girard-bred evergreen azalea from two unnamed white seedling parents, also sold as 'Girard Kathy'.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, mulching to protect the shallow root system from heat and drought. Kathy Ann bears flat-opening white flowers with slightly wavy-edged lobes on a compact, small-leaved evergreen shrub, a dependable Girard introduction bred from two unnamed white seedlings. It has also served as a breeding parent, passing its clean white color into later Girard-line crosses such as 'Pleasant White'. Prune only right after flowering finishes, since next year's buds set soon afterward, and feed with an acidic fertilizer formulated for azaleas and rhododendrons in early spring.

common_name: Clara Marie Azalea (Ruffled White Girard Evergreen Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Clara Marie is a Girard-bred evergreen azalea documented in Fred Galle's 1987 Azaleas and hardy to about -10F.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, mulching to protect the shallow root system from heat and drought. Clara Marie carries slightly ruffled white flowers about two and a half inches across on a dense, upright evergreen bush, one of the hardier Girard introductions for colder gardens. It has also been used as a breeding parent, contributing its white color to later Girard-line crosses such as 'Pleasant White'. Prune only right after flowering finishes, since next year's buds set soon afterward, and feed with an acidic azalea fertilizer in early spring.
